title: the same softdouble descriptor, re-labeled as an ordinary kernel, is accepted — the graph_block rejection only applies to the graph_block pattern
why: This is row10's fixture with `pattern` changed to an ordinary kernel
pattern and nothing else touched — same `softdouble` scalar_type, same
leftover graph_block-only keys. The existing float64 wire representation
already serves SoftDouble bit-identically, so an ordinary sidecar's
`scalar_type: softdouble` is accepted by the shared validator's general
dtype check; only the graph_block-specific check (pinned by row10) narrows this,
and that check never runs when the pattern is not `graph_block`.
The leftover graph_block-only keys ride along as unrecognized-but-harmless
top-level keys on an ordinary sidecar (schema v1 allows additional
properties) and prove the graph_block check triggers on the pattern value, not
merely on the presence of graph_block-looking keys.
Accepted at the shared validator only: past that gate, a launching loader
would proceed to load a stub artifact and fail for an unrelated reason,
which would prove nothing about validation.
